newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES SOFTER IN LIQUID MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES SOFTER IN LIQUID MARKET.

text.p: Short-term interest rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted largely softer in Wednesday's liquid and fairly active market.
"The market is slightly active today. There were some treasury bill maturities and everyone is trying to renew them," a dealer said.

He said discount houses were selling treasury bills on the market at 17.75 percent from Tuesday's 17.85 percent while NCD bills with maturity of 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at 19.25 percent and sold at 18 percent. On Tuesday they were selling at 18.50 percent.
Bankers acceptances eased to 18.25 and 17.75 percent (buying and selling respectively) from 18.50 and 17.85 percent the previous day but call money gained half a percentage point to 18.50 percent.
The market opened in surplus of Z$101.8 million, up from Z$40.6 million last time.
